title: Molarity

references.label: NCERT Chemistry Part I, Class 11 — Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

expression: M = n / V   (moles of solute per litre of SOLUTION)
explanation: Molarity expresses concentration as moles of solute per litre of total SOLUTION (not solvent). It is temperature-dependent, because the volume of a solution changes slightly with temperature (due to thermal expansion), even though the number of moles of solute stays fixed.

variables.unit: mol/L (also written mol dm⁻³ or M)

variables.meaning: Volume of the SOLUTION (not just solvent)

conditions: Temperature-dependent, since solution volume changes with temperature

workedExample.scenario: 2 moles of NaCl are dissolved to make 4 L of solution.

commonMistakes: Using the volume of SOLVENT added instead of the final volume of SOLUTION — these are only the same in dilute approximations, not in general.
Confusing molarity (mol/L of solution, temperature-dependent) with molality (mol/kg of solvent, temperature-independent) — a very common exam trap.
genZNote: Molarity and molality look like siblings on paper but behave completely differently once temperature changes — one shifts, one doesn't.
